sentences.text:
Ramchandra Soni vs Sunil on 11 March, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:7409
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Indore

BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE GAJENDRA SINGH  ON THE 11th OF MARCH, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 3256 of 2024  RAMCHANDRA SONI AND OTHERS  Versus  SUNIL AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Sajid Iqbal Ansari - advocate for the appellants  Shri Bhashkar Agrawal - Advocate for the respondent N  ORDER

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 27.06.2023 passed by Third MACT, Ujjain, District Ujjain in Claim Case No.437 of 2022 for enhancement of Rs.3,00,000/-.
2. Liabilities were not disputed, accordingly, the facts are being stated briefly.

In an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, a compensation of Rs..9,01,600/- was awarded for the death of Kamlesh Soni, who was Labour by profession, Son of appellant No.1 and brother of appellant Nos.2 and 4 and brother-in-law of appellant No.3.

The deceased was bachelor aged about twenty four years died on 06.04.2022 in a motor vehicular accident.
3. The Tribunal calculated loss of dependency assessing the income as Rs. 5,500/- per month and awarded the compensation as follows :-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:7409 2 MA-3256-2024 Income Rs.5,500 + 2200 (40% F.P)=Rs 7700 (per month) x 12 Loss of = Rs. 92,400- 1/2 (personal expenses) x 18 (Multiplier) = Rs.
dependency 8,31,600/-
Loss of Rs 40,000/-
Consortium Funeral Rs.15,000/-
Ramchandra Soni vs Sunil on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16191864/
1 expenses Loss of estate Rs 15,000/-
Total amount Rs 9,01,600/-
4.
This appeal has been preferred on the ground that per month income has been assessed on the lower side and there is a calculation mistake regarding loss of consortium.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
The counsel for the respondent opposed the prayer and submitted that awarded amount by the Tribunal is appropriate and proper.
No further interference is required.
7. The Tribunal ought to have assessed the per month income as Rs. 7000/- and 40% ought to have added for future prospect.
The tribunal ought to have awarded loss of dependency to all the appellants, at par.

On re- calculation, the compensation of loss of dependency comes to Rs.
11,34,000/-.
The Tribunal has assessed only Rs.8,31,600/-.
Hence, a sum of Rs.3,09,400/- is further enhanced.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
8. The appellant has valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.3,00,000/- and paid the Court fee accordingly.

However, for the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:7409 3 MA-3256-2024 remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellant within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months,
the claimant shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.
9. Accordingly, appeal is disposed of to the extent indicated herein above.
(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE rashmi Ramchandra Soni vs Sunil on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16191864/
